source.title: OFMU: Optimization-Driven Framework for Machine Unlearning

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The text gives conflicting publication dates: it says published at ICLR 2026, while the supplied metadata says ICLR and 2025.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates unlearning efficacy and retained utility for OFMU and baseline methods, using its own framework and benchmarks. It does not test recovery by fine-tuning, internal edits, or quantization.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates in-scope paraphrase, multi-hop, and cross-lingual prompts in Table 7; those results are recorded under E. It does not apply recovery fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization, or jailbreak attacks. The WMDP and TOFU tables report unlearning and utility metrics, not recovery attacks. Figures and tables about CIFAR, embedding similarity, difficulty, runtimes, and component ablations do not measure the claim versions directly.
record.test_reason: This is a new-method paper (OFMU). It runs no recovery attack, so it does not test shallowness under B–D. Its benchmark results still bear on part of A. On WMDP with Zephyr-7B-beta, forget accuracy for OFMU and RMU sits near the 25% four-choice chance level, with an MMLU subset reported (Table 5). The RMU rows rerun the original's own setting. TOFU utility is reported alongside Finetuned and Retrain references (Tables 1–2). Table 7 runs paraphrase, multi-hop and cross-lingual probes (E-type) but gives no canonical-prompt comparison, so it cannot show recovery for E or resistance for F.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that OFMU gives a state-of-the-art forgetting–utility trade-off across language and vision benchmarks, with better stability, robustness to hard-to-forget samples and resilience to membership inference. An appendix adds that it handles paraphrased, multi-hop and cross-lingual probes better than baselines. They run no relearning, ablation, quantization or jailbreak attack.
record.recipe_differences: OFMU is a new penalty-based bi-level optimization method; the study compares it with existing unlearning baselines rather than reproducing a listed original recovery-attack method.
record.method_sensitivity: TOFU results vary across forget ratios and model architectures. The paper also reports that in-scope prompt type affects its measured metrics, and that inner steps and penalty values affect forgetting and utility.

fits_no_version.finding: CIFAR-10/100 MIA-efficacy, and TOFU embedding similarity to Retrain on easy vs hard samples (Tables 3, 6, 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Membership-inference resistance and representation alignment of unlearned vision models and LLMs.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2026, as stated in the paper text)
record.problems: No recovery attacks are evaluated, and no chance-level reference is supplied for TOFU FQ or WMDP efficacy. TOFU FQ is described as higher-is-better in the tables, while the appendix defines FQ as degradation in accuracy or likelihood; the paper's prose also characterizes Gradient Ascent as strong forgetting despite extremely small tabulated FQ values. The prompt-transformation table has no canonical-prompt or unlearned-model comparison.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached. Omitted other TOFU methods and metrics (including GradDiff, NPO, SimNPO, preference methods, FTR), additional Table 7 methods and measures, and CIFAR-10/100 results. These were lower priority than rows covering both architectures, multiple forget ratios, retrain controls, the WMDP efficacy/utility comparison, and the tested prompt transformations.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the forgotten knowledge. TOFU forgetting relative to chance.
All; no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
All; no activation ablation or access-vs-deletion analysis.
Jailbreaks and in-context information. Also a comparison of rephrased against canonical prompts, which is needed to show recovery.

OFMU is never tested against relearning, ablation, quantization or jailbreak attacks. Its claimed robustness to paraphrase, multi-hop and cross-lingual probes (T55, T56, T57) has no canonical-prompt comparison.

missing.what: Finetuned (pre-unlearning) FQ/MU/FTR rows, which are the proper baselines for all TOFU rows (LLaMA-2 MU 0.64/0.63/0.64; LLaMA-3.2 MU 0.60 at all ratios)
WMDP NPO and SimNPO efficacy and MMLU values (NPO 68.8/64.9/72.8; SimNPO 68.9/66.2/73.3)
TOFU forget05 FQ/MU over five random forget-set draws (MU: RMU 0.58, OFMU 0.55, GA 0.18). This conflicts with Table 1's RMU MU of 0.02.

record.verdict_notes:
Changes from the earlier verdict:
(1) Expanded the list and range row_ids that the merge refused (T1,T3,…,T41 and T19-T24,T43-T48), and the T55-T60 range, into one item per row. Their links and states are unchanged.
(2) T16 and T18 (RMU, LLaMA-2, forget05/forget10 MU 0.02/0.03) changed from absent to cannot_determine and removed from the GA limits_scope label. The same paper gives RMU forget05 LLaMA-2 MU of 0.58 (Table 8) and 0.56–0.58 (Table 7), and its prose says RMU preserves utility well.
(3) Added T14 (RMU LLaMA-2 forget01 MU 0.62 vs 0.64, observed) to the TOFU-utility supports label; it had been left out of every label.
(4) Linked T55–T57 (OFMU under prompt transformations) to F as well as E: the authors claim OFMU resists these probes where baselines collapse. The state stays cannot_determine.
(5) Corrected the FQ remark. The paper's two FQ definitions both read as higher-is-better. The real inconsistency is that the tabled values (Retrain 1.00, values like 1e-119) look like TOFU KS-test p-values, and the prose says GA 'attains higher raw FQ' while its tabled FQ is the lowest.
(6) Removed the Table 7 missing entry, because rows_left_out declares 'additional Table 7 methods and measures'. Added Table 8 as missing.
(7) authors_conclusion no longer says the paper runs none of the claim's attacks: Table 7's probes are E-type.

Remaining inconsistencies: OFMU forget05 FQ is 0.14 in Table 1 but 0.44/0.41 in Tables 7/8. The prose says GradDiff collapses utility, yet Table 1 gives GradDiff MU 0.57–0.59. FTR is marked higher-is-better in the tables but defined as lower-is-better in Appendix 7.5.10. The WMDP 'Retrain' row gives below-chance forget accuracy (21.4% Bio) and MMLU-subset 82.4, and the paper never says how Zephyr-7B was retrained. The WMDP near-chance verdict rests on reading efficacy as 1 − accuracy on four-choice items, as the paper states. This study is not an original source. No instructions were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures forgetting and retained-utility outcomes, but does not test whether simple recovery attacks restore the targeted knowledge. It does not provide a chance-level reference for the reported TOFU FQ or WMDP efficacy measures.
No post-unlearning relearning or fine-tuning attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of whether unlearning blocks access rather than deletes knowledge is tested.

Tests paraphrase, multi-hop, and cross-lingual in-scope probes on TOFU, but not jailbreaks or in-context information. The reported FQ values are not compared with a no-transformation condition or a stated chance-level reference.
The paper does not test whether OFMU resists the recovery attacks named in the claim.

relationships.condition: OFMU and RMU on WMDP Bio/Cyber, Zephyr-7B-beta
relationships.reason: Forget-set accuracy (100 minus efficacy) is 27–32% against 25% chance (T49, T50, T52, T53). No pre-unlearning accuracy is given, and the attack-resistance part is untested.
relationships.display_finding: Forget-set accuracy reached 27–32% against 25% chance, without a pre-unlearning accuracy comparison or attack evaluation.

relationships.condition: MMLU-subset utility after WMDP unlearning, Zephyr-7B-beta (OFMU and RMU)
relationships.reason: MMLU is 74.6 (T51) and 74.2 (T54), about 8 points below the paper's Retrain reference of 82.4. That reference is not described, and no pre-unlearning MMLU is given.
relationships.display_finding: MMLU was 74.6 for OFMU and 74.2 for RMU versus the paper's retraining reference of 82.4.

relationships.condition: TOFU utility: OFMU at all forget ratios on LLaMA-2-7B and LLaMA-3.2-1B; RMU on LLaMA-3.2-1B and on LLaMA-2 forget01
relationships.reason: MU stays within 0.04 of Finetuned (0.60–0.64) (T2, T4, T6, T14, T26, T28, T30, T38, T40, T42). The forgetting level cannot be read against chance.
relationships.display_finding: Model utility stayed within 0.04 of the finetuned reference of 0.60–0.64, although forgetting could not be compared with chance.

relationships.condition: Gradient Ascent on TOFU, LLaMA-2-7B and LLaMA-3.2-1B
relationships.reason: MU collapses to 0.00 at forget05/forget10 (T10, T12, T34, T36) and drops at forget01 (0.55 vs Finetuned 0.64, T8; 0.35 vs 0.60, T32).
relationships.display_finding: Utility reached 0.00 for 5%/10% forget sets and fell to 0.55 versus 0.64 and 0.35 versus 0.60 for 1% forget sets.
